extracted.intended_audience: educated readers, poets, and literary critics interested in Milton and poetic criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Close critical commentary on books 4–5 of Milton's Paradise Lost, articulating standards for poetic diction, characterization, unity, use of the marvellous, allusion, and foreshadowing. Aimed at readers and writers of poetry who wish to understand what makes Milton's handling of these elements successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid continuous exaggerated flattery in character speech
rubrics_metrics.description: An injudicious Poet would have made Adam talk thro the whole Work in such Sentiments as these: But Flattery and Falshood are not the Courtship of Milton's Adam, and could not be heard by Eve in her State of Innocence, excepting only in a Dream produc'd on purpose to taint her Imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters should not constantly speak in overblown, flattering phrases inconsistent with their established nature; deviations (e.g., flattering speeches) must be plainly motivated (as by a dream) so they don't undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreshadow without anticipating the story
rubrics_metrics.description: Tho the Catastrophe of the Poem is finely presag'd on this Occasion, the Particulars of it are so artfully shadow'd, that they do not anticipate the Story which follows in the ninth Book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hints and presaging details to prepare the reader for future events, but avoid revealing particulars that would spoil later developments; foreshadowing should deepen interest, not remove suspense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dreams to justify aberrant or corrupting sentiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Eves Dream is full of those high Conceits engendring Pride... An injudicious Poet would have made Adam talk thro the whole Work in such Sentiments as these: But... could not be heard by Eve in her State of Innocence, excepting only in a Dream produc'd on purpose to taint her Imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a poet needs a character to express sentiments atypical for their nature, presenting them as a dream or vision can credibly account for such departures and preserve character consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allusion and imitation of authoritative sources enrich poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: I cannot but take notice that Milton, in the Conferences between Adam and Eve, had his Eye very frequently upon the Book of Canticles... I think there is no question but the Poet in the preceding Speech remember'd those two Passages which are spoken on the like occasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-chosen allusions—to Scripture, Homer, or other classical sources—can deepen meaning and aesthetic effect; explicit parallels (e.g., to Canticles or Homer) justify and illuminate images and passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground marvellous elements in precedent or authority
rubrics_metrics.description: As Milton every where fills his Poem with Circumstances that are marvellous and astonishing... I will not pretend to determine, whether in this particular of Homer the Marvellous does not lose sight of the Probable. As the miraculous Workmanship of Milton's Gates is not so extraordinary as this of the Tripodes, so I am persuaded he would not have mentioned it, had not he been supported in it by a Passage in the Scripture...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extraordinary or marvellous descriptions should be defensible by precedent or authority (e.g., Scripture, classical epic); doing so prevents the marvellous from sacrificing plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve unity of action
rubrics_metrics.description: Whichever of the Notions be true, the Unity of Milton's Action is preserved according to either of them; whether we consider the Fall of Man in its immediate Beginning, as proceeding from the Resolutions taken in the infernal Council, or in its more remote Beginning, as proceeding from the first Revolt of the Angels in Heaven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the narrative's effective starting-point can be argued differently, the poem should maintain an overall unity of action so that the plot coheres whether read from one perspective or another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character behaviour must suit their dignity and given character
rubrics_metrics.description: Raphael's Behaviour is every way suitable to the Dignity of his Nature, and to that Character of a sociable Spirit, with which the Author has so judiciously introduced him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions, speech, and demeanor must align with the character's established status and nature (e.g., angelic dignity, heroic loyalty); this appropriateness reinforces believability and thematic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use natural transitions between topics and speeches
rubrics_metrics.description: After having thus entered into Conversation with Man upon more indifferent Subjects, he warns him of his Obedience, and makes natural Transition to the History of that fallen Angel...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifts in subject should arise organically from previous discourse; transitions that feel forced will weaken persuasive or narrative impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate ordinary subjects through pleasing images and strong expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Though in this, and other Parts of the same Book, the Subject is only the Housewifry of our first Parent, it is set off with so many pleasing Images and strong Expressions, as make it none of the least agreeable Parts in this Divine Work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even prosaic domestic scenes can be rendered poetically by employing apt imagery and expressive language; treatment can make 'housewifry' compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Render grand scenes with force of imagination and variety
rubrics_metrics.description: The Revolt in Heaven is described with great Force of Imagination and a fine Variety of Circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Epic or monumental episodes should be depicted with imaginative energy and a rich variety of circumstances to sustain interest and convey scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid, lively descriptive colour to depict person and place
rubrics_metrics.description: Raphael's Descent to the Earth, with the Figure of his Person, is represented in very lively Colours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific, lively descriptive detail (colour, movement, fragrance) helps make supernatural or sublime figures tangible and memorable to the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide moral exemplars through character portrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Part of Abdiel, who was the only Spirit that in this infinite Host of Angels preserved his Allegiance to his Maker, exhibits to us a noble Moral of religious Singularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters may be crafted to model moral virtues (e.g., loyalty, intrepidity); their speech and actions should illustrate and reinforce the moral point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate heroic diction and warmth of sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Zeal of the Seraphim breaks forth in a becoming Warmth of Sentiments and Expressions, as the Character which is given us of him denotes that generous Scorn and Intrepidity which attends Heroic Virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heroic or elevated characters should speak with a tone and warmth suitable to their virtue; diction must match the moral and emotional weight of heroic actions.
